A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GEM/GEM-S metrics and GRE-bench study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and additional experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-grade correlations, degradation and manipulation experiments, GRE-bench model evaluations, and fine-tuning experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds alternative-preprocessing experiments, Yelp evaluations, DeepSeek scores, and an empirical probability-consistency analysis.

M1.justification: The GEM/GEM-S equations, probability estimation, preprocessing pipeline, and fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. Testing another preprocessing model and using restaurant categories as the existing synopsis input do not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds Yelp restaurant reviews, extending evaluation beyond academic proposals and paper reviews to customer judgments about businesses. It also tests reviews replaced by reviews of different restaurants. The academic datasets remain.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons use the same BLEU, ROUGE-L, BERTScore, BARTScore variants, and GPT-4o LMExaminer baselines. Yelp introduces no new baseline method. The added DeepSeek models are candidates assessed by GRE-bench, rather than competing evaluation methods.

E3.justification: New experimental settings include Llama-3.2-90B preprocessing, Yelp sampling with review-length filters and category conditioning, and a probability-consistency diagnostic using 500 papers and 5,328 review pairs. These expand the evaluation design; newly disclosed parsing and decoding details do not establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 tests dependence on the preprocessing model and identifies two manipulation failures. Appendix A.4 adds restaurant-review degradation and rephrasing tests, including random replacement. Appendix A.5 investigates consistency between opposite probability factorizations. The earlier fine-tuning analysis remains in Appendix E.

E5.justification: Both versions report Spearman p-values, 95% confidence intervals for degradation/manipulation effects, and 90% intervals in GRE-bench figures. The fine-tuning seed remains 42. Additional result tables follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice, without new repeated-run counts or interval-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds DeepSeek scores, preprocessing and Yelp results, and a probability-consistency correlation of 0.943. With Llama preprocessing, GEM increases under Llama rephrasing and elongation by SMDs of 0.124 and 0.138, exposing failures under that additional setting. Section 5 also changes the reported GEM/GEM-S(ASSW) cross-evaluator correlations from 0.90/0.93 to 0.93/0.90. Original tabulated results are retained.

T1.justification: The mutual-information definitions, assumptions, Proposition 3.1, Proposition B.1, and their proofs are substantively unchanged. Appendix A.5 empirically examines a standard probability identity rather than adding a theorem or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same claims about reference-based evaluation without gold standards, alignment with human judgments, manipulation resistance, and GRE-bench. The additional experiments support or qualify these existing claims rather than redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications concerning preprocessing quality, imperfect probability consistency, PDF-parsing limitations, and unofficial parameter-size estimates. It removes v1's discussion of why ordinary fine-tuning may be unsuitable for subjective judgments, while retaining the fine-tuning results. The principal limitations concerning estimation accuracy and human-generated references remain.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility documentation: temperature 0, a 4,000-token output limit, Sciencebeam parsing and content exclusions, context-length checks, evaluation hardware, and Colab requirements. It also explains missing benchmark-score handling. These are disclosures, not evidence of rerunning existing experiments. Conversely, v1's explicit sentence-level BERTScore segmentation detail is omitted.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to peer prediction, mutual-information estimation, and NLG evaluation remain unchanged. Citation formatting changes do not add a new research relationship.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose is retained, with localized rewrites and revised future-work discussion. v2 adds a reproducibility statement, consolidates GRE-bench appendix material, and reorders Appendix D. This is limited narrative reorganization rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR layout and extensively reflows the title, figures, tables, and prompt boxes. Figure 5 gains DeepSeek bars and a different color palette. Five new result tables are added, while the existing benchmark-correlation table and validation algorithm are duplicated in appendices. Figures 1–4 and 6 retain their underlying graphics.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides useful evidence beyond academic reviewing, exposes preprocessing-dependent failure conditions, and fills important reproducibility gaps. These improve the paper's evidential support and transparency. The gains are tempered by reporting inconsistencies, including Appendix A.3 quoting the original GEM correlation as 0.433 while the unchanged Table 1 reports 0.431.
